chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him: At what amount is the thief's hand cut off? He said: "Its minimum is one-third of a dīnār."

So the proper way regarding this report is that it is not impossible that this was a description of a particular case about which he, peace be upon him, was asked, namely that for which Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام carried out the cutting, and so it was said to the questioner: one-third of a dīnār; and that it is not a report stating that this is its fixed limit in all circumstances.

What clarifies that is that Samāʿah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام the story of the egg whose thief Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام had punished by cutting, and he mentioned that its value was one-quarter of a dīnār.
And what further increases that in clarity is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose judicial action is cited here
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief subject to the ruling of theft
key_terms.ثُلُثِ دِينَارٍ: one-third of a dīnār as the amount mentioned in this report
key_terms.رُبُعَ دِينَارٍ: one-quarter of a dīnār mentioned in another related report
key_terms.قِصَّةَ الْبَيْضَةِ: the incident of the egg used as clarifying evidence

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount for the hadd punishment of theft in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal threshold for applying the hadd punishment for theft and presents a report mentioning one-third of a dīnār. It then explains that this wording may refer to a specific incident rather than a universal rule, especially since another report from the same narrator mentions a case involving one-quarter of a dīnār.
